objections.claim: D-025 records the three Route C forms only as a non-exclusive census of forms this corpus has used and rejects inventing a new closed consumption set.
objections.evidence: The provenance qualifier does not make the operative rule open. Decision 3 still says a Route C decision is 'recorded in one of these forms,' then requires a successor or supersession to change the enumeration. That makes the three examples exhaustive for live work even though D-001 section 3 names only the product-disposition process and establishes no closed carrier census. D-025's own Alternatives section says a new closed set was rejected, and Decision 5 says D-001 is not amended. Removing 'exactly one' permits multiple listed records to co-occur, but it does not permit a lawful fourth recording form without first amending D-025.
objections.proposedFix: Make the list genuinely illustrative: say 'including, but not limited to, the following corpus-used forms' and remove the enumeration-successor clause. A newly proposed carrier still must derive authority from the product-disposition process, D-000, or the user; if the intent is instead to freeze an exhaustive three-form set, classify and justify that novel governance choice rather than calling it a RULE-GOVERNED restatement.

objections.claim: D-027 states the authoritative DR-004 work that remains owed, and D-031 consistently starts all outstanding D-001 Route A work while leaving file-11 item 7 unscheduled and declaring that these entries do not start the section-3.1 instrument.
objections.evidence: D-001 section 3 defines DR-004 Route A as two obligations: the exact eight-bullet Phase-1A packet 'plus commission the missing section-3.1-item-to-supplier binding instrument.' D-027 Decision 3, its Route A alternative, and its honesty paragraph reserve only the packet. D-031 says Lane R is all outstanding authoritative-path work under D-001 and starts with adoption, but its file-11 accounting leaves item 7 unscheduled; file 11 item 7 is exactly the section-3.1 supplier-coverage instrument. The final disclaimer then expressly says these entries do not start that instrument. The universal Lane R sentence prevents a formal waiver, but the specific scheduling and disclaimer bytes point the other way and leave D-027's dual track incomplete.
objections.proposedFix: Add the supplier-binding instrument to D-027's authoritative reservation. In D-031, state that the instrument is already standing Route A work by D-001 and place its authoring in Lane R, while distinguishing that from file 11's lack of authority. Remove item 7 from the unscheduled/not-started set, or narrow Lane R and record the actual deprioritization trade explicitly.

objections.claim: The new entries preserve the predecessor-status relation to the CONTESTED D-019 through D-024 decisions when adopted.
objections.evidence: Turn 1 explicitly marked D-026, D-027, D-028, D-029, D-030, and D-031 as superseding CONTESTED D-019, D-020, D-021, D-022, D-023, and D-024 respectively. Turn 2 deletes all six lines while retaining D-025's supersession of D-017. The common Predecessor field names only the turn-1 draft, not the six contested decisions, and the entries are declared severable. D-000's register has a SUPERSEDED status and the current contested-cycle record calls D-025 through D-031 successors; adoption without the per-entry mapping leaves the old six decisions parked CONTESTED beside their replacements and makes the asymmetric D-025 mapping unexplained.
objections.proposedFix: Restore the six per-entry Supersedes lines, and make each adoption record move only its mapped contested predecessor to SUPERSEDED. Preserve severability: adopting or overturning one successor must not change the status of the other five predecessor entries.

objections.claim: D-029's preference-honesty and readiness-effect text accurately describe what adoption enables.
objections.evidence: Decision 5 says D-029 writes no disposition and authorizes no blueprint, and Readiness effect says zero at adoption. The Honesty section nevertheless states as the gain that 'scoped design of non-authoritative doctor/purge can proceed.' Unlike D-026, D-027, and D-030, D-029 deleted the sentence explaining that only a later completed, reviewed, owner-recorded disposition may discharge scoped condition 1 and that conditions 2 through 5 remain. The gain therefore reads as an immediate consequence of the selector even though the entry's own operative and readiness text deny that consequence.
objections.proposedFix: Say that adoption permits authoring the later disposition, not preview design. Restore the per-entry effect sentence: only after a completed, reviewed, evidence/retention-authority-recorded disposition may condition 1 be discharged within its scope, and conditions 2 through 5 remain independently required.

objections.claim: D-031 remains totally reversible by supersession plus one git revert even after its ordered drafting and decision steps execute.
objections.evidence: D-031 authorizes drafting across five ordered steps, including later product decisions, register mechanics, routed defects, five Route B dispositions, and two product contracts. After any resulting artifact travels A, B, or C, reverting C-D031 can stop the sequence prospectively but cannot undo the historical order, incurred work, or independently live downstream decisions. The selector entries now state exactly this temporal boundary for their dependents, while D-031 labels its own reversibility unconditionally total and names only D-018 and D-025 through D-030 as survivors.
objections.proposedFix: State that one-revert total reversal exists only before execution begins. After dependent work or decisions land, supersession is prospective; independently live downstream acts remain standing unless separately overturned under their own procedures. Name that cost in the preference trade instead of implying history and dependents disappear with C-D031.

objections.claim: D-031 satisfies D-000 clause 3 and clause 5 preference honesty for the chosen five-step order and two-lane concurrency.
objections.evidence: The only stated loss is that neither lane is the unique critical path; the only stated gain is parallelism. That does not record parallelism's material cost—shared coordinator/owner capacity, work-in-progress contention, and the risk that preview drafting outruns authoritative closure—or explain why steps 1 through 5 are ordered as written. The only effort-model alternative is rejected 'as a blocker of these entries,' which is circular: whether missing effort data should block this preference choice is the question, not a reason against it. File 11 itself records that no reader can tell whether the slice is a quarter or a multi-year program because no row estimates cost.
objections.proposedFix: Record why this ordering is robust without estimates, the capacity/WIP trade of parallel lanes, and what preempts what when owners conflict. Either schedule a lightweight effort/critical-path view before or in parallel with the sequence, or justify proceeding without it on the merits; do not reject the evidence merely because it could change the decision.
